title: Life Sciences CRM Platform Architecture Patterns and Packaging Strategy
summary: Architectural patterns for building life sciences CRM on managed package platforms, including packaging structure, API design, trigger architecture, and admin console decisions drawn from production implementations with 550+ custom objects and multi-package deployments.

findings.packaging_structure: Mature life sciences CRM implementations partition functionality across multiple second-generation managed packages (8-12 packages in enterprise deployments). Each package owns a bounded domain (e.g., consent, samples, events, CLM) with explicit cross-package dependencies declared in sfdx-project.json.
findings.composite_api_pattern: Cross-package data operations use composite API patterns to maintain transactional integrity. A single user action (e.g., completing a visit with sample drops, call notes, and signature capture) may touch objects across 3-4 packages and must be orchestrated through a shared API layer.
findings.trigger_vs_platform_events: Two architectural approaches for cross-package communication: (1) trigger-based with shared utility classes — simpler but creates tight coupling; (2) platform event-based — decoupled but adds latency and eventual consistency complexity. Production implementations often use a hybrid: triggers for synchronous operations, platform events for asynchronous workflows.
findings.admin_console_design: A centralized admin console (custom setup application) consolidates configuration across packages. This avoids requiring administrators to navigate individual package setup screens. The console reads/writes custom settings and custom metadata types that each package consumes.
findings.key_strategic_decisions: Critical architecture decisions that cascade through the implementation: (a) managed vs. unlocked packages — managed for ISV distribution, unlocked for internal apps; (b) namespace strategy — consistent prefixes enable cross-package references; (c) custom metadata vs. custom settings — metadata for deployable config, settings for org-specific runtime config.
findings.scale_considerations: At scale (50K+ users, 100M+ records), the architecture must account for: bulk API governor limits, sharing rule performance, platform cache usage for frequently accessed reference data, and async processing for heavy compute operations.

source: Consolidated from CRM platform architecture presentations covering managed package design, composite APIs, and large-scale deployment patterns
